title: IC 2944, nicknamed the Running Chicken Nebula
caption: The Running Chicken Nebula, IC 2944, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: IC 2944 · constellation Centaurus · about 6500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Taken with the Wide Field Imager camera on La Silla's 2.2-meter MPG/ESO telescope, this view features the Running Chicken Nebula, a gas cloud with young stars inside it, lying around 6500 light-years away in the constellation of Centaurus (the Centaur).

Its official names are IC 2944 and the Lambda Centauri Nebula. The odd nickname comes from the shape of its brightest region, which some people see as a bird. The star Lambda Centauri, which gives the nebula one of its names, sits just outside the field of view.

Clouds like this are where stars form. Gas and dust collapse into new stars, and those young stars then light up the surrounding gas with their energetic radiation. The telescope recorded the scene through blue, visual and red filters plus one that isolates the glow of hydrogen, which is especially good at picking out gas energized by young stars. The official caption gives few further details.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (34.01 x 30.77 arcminutes) and distance (6500 light years), the frame spans roughly 64 × 58 light-years. Its light set out about 6,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and R filters with a hydrogen-alpha filter. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the nebula appears much brighter and more colorful here than through an eyepiece.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

alt: A cloud of glowing gas and newborn stars, its brightest region shaped somewhat like a bird.
